summary: Google DeepMind announced that computer use is now a built-in tool natively integrated into Gemini 3.5 Flash, previously only available as a standalone Gemini 2.5 computer use model, along with new enterprise safeguard features.

mechanisms.reason: The lab states the built-in tool lets developers build agents that act across browser, mobile and desktop environments for long-horizon automation tasks.
mechanisms.quote: This unlocks improved performance for long-horizon and enterprise automation tasks like continuous software testing and knowledge work across professional applications.

practices.reason: Computer use is now natively supported in the main Flash model with improved agentic performance, giving teams a built-in option for agent tasks previously requiring a separate model.
practices.quote: Computer use is now a built-in tool supported in Gemini 3.5 Flash, delivering our best performance yet for agentic computer use tasks.

practices.reason: The tool gives a concrete, API-accessible pattern for building agents that see, reason and act across environments, replacing the need for a standalone model.
practices.quote: With built-in computer use capability, developers can now use 3.5 Flash to reliably build custom agents that can see, reason and take action across browser, mobile and desktop environments.

practices.reason: The lab describes concrete safety techniques and optional safeguard controls a team could apply when deploying computer-use agents.
practices.quote: To mitigate some of the prompt injection risks for agents operating in live environments, we use targeted adversarial training for computer use in Gemini 3.5 Flash.

practices.reason: Developers gain a new API surface for computer use within the existing Flash model rather than a breaking change or deprecation.
practices.quote: Developers and enterprises can start using computer use in 3.5 Flash via the Gemini API and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform .
